answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a market or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a bonded challenge proves the identity is duplicating an existing participant. A basalt ledger records deposits and penalties, while a beacon publishes challenge deadlines so honest agents can respond. Sybils cannot gain influence for free: the attacker must lock real capital across many accounts and risks losing it, making a spiral of identities increasingly costly.
